prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1359; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Pearland, Texas, I found a two-vehicle collision. Driver 2 was attempting a left turn across oncoming traffic when the front of their vehicle struck the side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported a fractured wrist from the impact and stated they had remained behind the wheel throughout. Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle, and both Driver 1 and Passenger confirmed this to me. No independent witnesses came forward. The force of the collision appears consistent with the injury Driver 1 described. Scene photographs show some of the damage the drivers described, but I could not determine whether all of the visible damage resulted from this impact. Vehicle records checked during the investigation show similar major damage to Driver 1's vehicle from an earlier incident that was never reported to police. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the vehicle.
